grok._note: Grok validates its OIDC session locally and rejects any placeholder (measured). Fallback tier: the access token is written into the sandbox (refresh stripped), --unshare-net and the broker's path/model/ceiling retained. Proven live 2026-08-18.

codex._note: ChatGPT subscription path. Needs a ChatGPT-Account-ID header (chatgpt_account_id claim). No adapter/pin yet -> cannot run live. Capture a real stream first.

claude._note: Claude subscription OAuth. Token goes in ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -> Authorization: Bearer (measured); ANTHROPIC_API_KEY would select the BYOK x-api-key path instead. Claude posts to /v1/messages?beta=true, so the broker matches the path component and ignores the query.

_note: This registry is CONTROLLER-OWNED and is the only source of model family /
vendor identity. A project profile may name ids from here; it can never
declare a family, because that would let a profile manufacture reviewer
independence.
This registry catalogues what the rail KNOWS, not what it can REACH. The
openrouter/* ids below are a curated starting set: they are NOT verified
against OpenRouter's live catalog (ids there change), and as of 2026-08-18
no OpenRouter credential is installed on this machine, so every one of them
is unreachable. They fail closed, loudly -- `ai-opencode models` marks each
id reachable or UNREACHABLE and names where its credential belongs, and a
job that asks for a live provider with no credential refuses rather than
running unbrokered. Add or remove entries freely: that is the intended way
to extend the pool.
Measured availability on opencode-go (2026-08-18): deepseek-v4-flash ok,
deepseek-v4-pro ok, kimi-k3 ok, qwen3.8-max flaky, glm-5.3 fails upstream.
vendor_family is what makes cross-vendor review independence meaningful.
Two openrouter models from the same vendor are NOT independent reviewers.
grok/* reaches the native Grok CLI. Everything about it below is MEASURED:
the id is the WIRE name the CLI puts in the request body (grok-4.6), not the
grok-4.6-build that its own modelUsage reports -- pinning the reported name
would have made the broker deny every request. Its paths came from pointing
GROK_CLI_BASE_URL at a recording server: POST /chat/completions, POST
/responses, and GET /models, which the CLI calls before any inference.
